current_title: Rainfall-associated frog chorus activation is concentrated within taxa across multiple sites

exact_NK_secondary.caveat: taxa are exchangeable conditional on N and K; intrinsic taxon spatial breadth and prior site use are not preserved

exploration_boundary.external_prospective_replication_require: independent confirmation only; not required for the current exploratory manuscript or submission

claim_spine.biological: strong chorus state switching -> excess within-taxon multi-site concentration -> recurrent species-specific physical-site placement
claim_spine.conceptual: short behavioural responses have separable response-magnitude and realised-configuration properties; in NAAMP the latter is taxon-concentrated, spatially selective and historically anchored

novelty_boundary.preferred_claim: conditional realised configuration of frog reproductive acoustic activity after response magnitude and explicit taxon/site propensities are represented

spatial_blocked_transferability.boundary: species rainfall response excludes the focal State; strictly-prior local site history, broader taxonomic support and observed activation magnitude remain conditioned on

temporal_blocked_transferability.boundary: species response and physical-site history frozen through 2008; response magnitude and broader taxonomic support remain conditioned on

future_rain_negative_control.interpretation: both antecedent and future amount models leave the concentration excess; their similar same-seed predictions do not support interpreting the incremental 72-h rainfall-amount fit as antecedent-specific

prior_knowledge: frog calling responds to weather and season
species x wetland calling structure and recurrent site use can persist
knowledge_shift.empirical_update: Short behavioural responses have at least two separable empirical properties: response magnitude and realised configuration. The same amount of activation can be realised through different taxon-by-place patterns.
frog_system_expression: excess within-taxon multi-site concentration after first-order comparators
deep spatial tail dominated by CI2/3
preferential expression at recurrent taxon-specific strong-chorus locations
knowledge_shift.transferability_update: The conditional configuration excess persists under focal-State-excluded response calibration and a 2009-2015 temporal block trained on response/history through 2008.
knowledge_shift.mechanism_narrowing: Antecedent and future 72-h rainfall-amount models give similar predictions while both leave the focal residual; the robust contribution is spatial organization, not a uniquely antecedent rainfall-amount mechanism.
knowledge_shift.general_ecological_hypothesis: Environmental-response studies may lose ecological information when they reduce a multivariate response to magnitude alone; realised configuration can be a second empirical axis of response.
boundaries: not individual movement, memory or philopatry

literature_verified_axes: rainfall amount, recency and lag windows
water chemistry as a lower-priority system-specific axis
social / prior-calling state as a biotic contextual driver
directly_or_strongly_addressed: generic contemporaneous stop-night condition shared across taxa
uniform species x route-night latent-state sufficiency
indirectly_addressed: vapour pressure deficit partly through temperature/humidity-related structure but not directly parameterized
static taxon-specific site quality through strictly-prior species x SiteID propensity
generic route-order/time progression through stop-night hotness and route-position diagnostics

not_directly_measured_ranked.family: dynamic local hydrology x taxon-specific breeding requirements
taxon-specific diel timing x route progression
local microclimate or moonlight x canopy/topography
examples: route-wide lunar cue requires local modifier to explain site selectivity

not_directly_measured_ranked.family: static habitat descriptors or water chemistry as sole explanation

environmental_factor_coverage.structural_constraint: Any omitted environmental explanation capable of reproducing the focal residual must vary among survey events, be non-uniform among stops, have taxon-specific effects, and preserve or reinforce recurrent taxon-specific site selectivity.
environmental_factor_coverage.leading_unresolved_environmental_alterna: dynamic, spatially heterogeneous local wetland state, especially hydroperiod/water level/inundation, local wetness/runoff/substrate moisture and water temperature, with taxon-specific effects
environmental_factor_coverage.completeness_verdict: Broad environmental coverage is strong, but exhaustive causal exclusion is impossible because direct site x survey-event wetland state was not measured.
environmental_factor_coverage.authorized_claim: Most major broad atmospheric, seasonal and observation-process explanations were directly or indirectly examined and were insufficient; all environmental causes have not been excluded.
environmental_factor_coverage.future_decisive_test: directly measure local wetland state in an independent repeated fixed-site system and compare broad-weather/phenology, local-state-only, and broad-state x local-filter generators
environmental_factor_coverage.science_lock: No new same-data hydrological, diel-timing or microclimate outcome analysis is authorized by this audit.
verified_literature_updates: Leung et al. 2026: humidity, wind, moonlight, canopy, lentic/temporary water and prior calling matter, with climate-zone-dependent importance
Pouso et al. 2026: photoperiod and temperature supported; rainfall and pressure unsupported in a subtropical permanent-pond system
Hainan 2026 thermal PAM study: diel partitioning and habitat-specific thermal responses
Rush et al. 2026: rainfall, minimum temperature and VPD effects differ strongly between nearby regions, consistent with local buffering/hydrology
Larsen et al. 2021: snowmelt and temperature track wood-frog breeding/calling phenology
Wheeler et al. 2018: water depth and water temperature influence calling phenology
Sarker et al. 2022: inundation produces species- and site-specific chorus changes
Mitchell 2001: experimentally wetter substrate increases male calling
